title: Etale source-and-target locality of the scheme Koszul lci condition
statement: For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $P(f)$ mean that every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which $f$ factors as a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], followed by a smooth morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $P$ is invariant under isomorphisms and etale local on source-and-target in the sense of [def-sfb-etale-local-source-target-property], where etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Explicitly, (i) $P(f)$ implies $P(fa)$ whenever $a:U\to X$ is etale; (ii) $P(f)$ implies $P(X\times_YV\to V)$ whenever $V\to Y$ is etale [def-pc-fibre-product]; (iii) $P(f)$ holds if and only if for every $x\in X$ there are schemes $U,V$, etale maps $a:U\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, and a morphism $h:U\to V$ satisfying $fa=bh$ and $P(h)$. No Noetherian, separation, quasi-compactness, or flatness hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Preamble to Tag 06C4 (definition-lci), which states etale source-and-target locality, from more-morphisms.tex Tags 069N (lemma-descending-property-lci), 069P (lemma-lci-syntomic-local-source), and descent.tex Tag 04R2 (lemma-etale-local-source-target).

proof.text: Work with the property $P$ as stated. Its witnesses restrict to source opens: restrict the closed immersion to an open of its source and then restrict the ambient scheme to an open on which it is closed; the smooth map restricts by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], and near each point of the restricted closed subscheme the ideal is still generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence on a smaller affine open by [new-s3-koszul-regular-affine-refinement] (points of the ambient open outside the closed subscheme have unit ideal, generated by the Koszul-regular sequence $1$). Such witnesses therefore glue as a property on an open cover of the source. For an open $V\subseteq Y$, restrict a witness through $Q\to Y$ to $Q\times_YV$, an open of $Q$; conversely compose its smooth map to $V$ with $V\hookrightarrow Y$, which is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]; the composite is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Thus $P(f|_{f^{-1}V}:f^{-1}V\to V)$ is equivalent to $P$ on that source open with target $Y$. Isomorphisms carry the same affine ideals and Koszul complexes to isomorphic ones, so they preserve the witnesses. These observations also show that an immersion which is locally Koszul-regular followed by a smooth map gives $P$: locally replace the immersion by a closed immersion into an ambient open.

source.place: Tag 069F (definition-lci), locality of the defining factorizations

proof.text: Every morphism with $P$ is locally of finite type. Indeed, locally its ambient smooth map is given by a finitely presented algebra, hence by finitely many algebra generators; taking a quotient for the closed immersion leaves finitely many generators. These assertions use the definitions in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-weil-closed-immersion], and [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Conversely, for any locally finite type $f$, choose affine neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and $B$ generated by $n$ elements over $A$. Sending the polynomial variables to these generators gives a surjection $A[t_1,\ldots,t_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$, hence a closed immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_V$. Its ambient map is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. More generally, if $P(f)$ and $j:U\to Q$ is any immersion over $Y$ into a smooth $Y$-scheme, compare $j$ at each point with a defining witness for $P$ using [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-smooth-ambient-independence]. It follows that $j$ is Koszul-regular. In particular this applies to the polynomial embeddings just constructed, after composing their ambient smooth maps with $V\hookrightarrow Y$ as in step 1.

source.place: Tags 069E, 069F and 069G; affine polynomial presentation described before Definition 069F

proof.text: Let $b:V\to Y$ be etale and assume $P(f)$. Pull back each local factorization $U\hookrightarrow Q\to Y$ to $V$. The pulled-back smooth morphism is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2). The map $Q\times_YV\to Q$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], hence flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Therefore the pulled-back closed immersion is Koszul-regular by [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-flat-ascent-etale-descent](1). The inverse images of the witness source opens cover $X\times_YV$, and step 1 converts their local Koszul-regular immersions into the required closed-immersion witnesses. This proves (ii).

Let $a:T\to X$ be etale and assume $P(f)$. Fix $t\in T$. Shrink a witness $U\hookrightarrow Q\to Y$ around $a(t)$ so that $Q$ is affine; its inverse image $U$ is affine since it is closed in $Q$. Choose an affine open $T_0\subseteq a^{-1}(U)$ containing $t$; the induced map $T_0\to U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2),(3), since $T_0\hookrightarrow T\xrightarrow{a}X$ is etale and $U\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-closed-immersion-lift] to $U\hookrightarrow Q$ and $T_0\to U$: it gives an affine etale $W\to Q$ and a cartesian square $T_0=U\times_QW$. The immersion $T_0\hookrightarrow W$ is Koszul-regular by [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-flat-ascent-etale-descent](1), since an etale map is flat. Also $W\to Y$ is smooth: $W\to Q$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], and use [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. These are witnesses for $P(fa)$ at every $t$, proving (i).

source.place: Tag 069P (lemma-lci-syntomic-local-source), etale specialization of the ambient lifting argument; algebra.tex lemma-lift-etale

proof.text: If $h:T\to V$ has $P$ and $b:V\to Y$ is etale, the same closed-immersion witnesses prove $P(bh)$: their ambient smooth maps to $V$, composed with the smooth map $b$, are smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] and [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. If $P(f)$, take $T=X$, $V=Y$ and both chart maps identities to obtain the witnesses in (iii) at every $x$. It remains to prove the reverse implication of (iii).

source.place: Tag 04R2 (lemma-etale-local-source-target), reduction to postcomposition and source descent

proof.text: Assume the pointwise chart condition of (iii). Step 5 gives $P(fa_x)$ for each chosen chart $a_x:T_x\to X$, and the points $u_x$ show that these etale maps jointly cover $X$. By step 2 each $fa_x$ is locally of finite type; source locality for this property in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] gives that $f$ is locally of finite type. Fix affine $V\subseteq Y$ and affine $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$ as in step 2, with polynomial closed immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Q=\mathbf A^n_V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], the charts $T_x\times_XU\to U$ form a jointly surjective etale family. Refine their sources by affine opens $T_\alpha$; each $T_\alpha\to U$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2), and they are still jointly surjective. Step 1 restricts $P(fa_x)$ to these opens, and restricts its target to $V$, giving $P(T_\alpha\to V)$. No claim that $f$ is flat is used.

source.place: Tag 069P, affine-source reduction and choice of a polynomial closed immersion; source descent for locally finite type

proof.text: Lift each affine etale $T_\alpha\to U$ across $j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-closed-immersion-lift], giving etale $q_\alpha:W_\alpha\to Q$ and $T_\alpha=U\times_QW_\alpha$. The map $W_\alpha\to V$ is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres], and [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. Since $P(T_\alpha\to V)$, step 2 shows that its closed immersion into $W_\alpha$ is Koszul-regular. Let $O=\bigcup_\alpha q_\alpha(W_\alpha)\subseteq Q$. It is open by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map], and it contains $j(U)$ because the $T_\alpha$ cover $U$. Thus $U\hookrightarrow O$ is a closed immersion; the maps $W_\alpha\to O$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], since $W_\alpha=W_\alpha\times_QO$, and jointly surjective, and their pullbacks of this immersion are exactly $T_\alpha\hookrightarrow W_\alpha$. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-immersion-flat-ascent-etale-descent](2) to conclude that $U\hookrightarrow O$ is Koszul-regular. As $O\to V$ is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], this gives $P(f|_U)$, and composing to $Y$ uses step 1. Such $U$ cover $X$, so $P(f)$ holds. For empty $X$ the condition and conclusion are both vacuous. Together with steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 this proves all assertions, and hence the property of [def-sfb-etale-local-source-target-property].
